AI spending just crossed a line that every executive needs to see.

Gartner's July 2026 forecast puts worldwide AI platforms and models spending at $64 billion this year — a 63.4% increase from $39 billion in 2025. GenAI model spending specifically is growing at 117%. These are not projections about some distant future. This is capital being allocated right now, at infrastructure scale.

What makes this particularly significant for business leaders: Gartner explicitly states that the long-term winners will not be the companies building the biggest models. The winners will be organizations that master governance, orchestration, and strategic deployment — managing where and how AI is used across every function of the business.

That distinction matters enormously. It means the competitive advantage does not belong to whoever spends the most. It belongs to whoever spends most intelligently. And that requires a coherent AI strategy at the leadership level — not scattered pilots across departments.

The parallel to cloud migration is striking. Five years ago, organizations without a cloud strategy were scrambling. Today, organizations without a unified AI deployment strategy face the same risk, only the timeline is compressed.
